t: By His Wounds We Have Peace
v: But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
b: This is an awe-inspiring passage. It tells us that Jesus Christ died for our sins, and through His suffering we receive peace and healing. In this troubled world we often feel confused, worried, and afraid, but this passage reminds us that if we believe in the redemption of Jesus, we can have true peace.

There was a young woman who lived in an environment full of pressure and difficulty. Every day she felt exhausted and could not withstand the challenges and pressures. But one day she heard the message of the redemption of Jesus Christ, and an inexpressible peace came into her heart. From that day she learned to hand her worries and difficulties over to Jesus and to believe that He can bring true peace.

Each of us may face all kinds of challenges and difficulties, and sometimes we even feel that life has lost its hope. But this passage reminds us that Jesus suffered for us on the cross. He bore our iniquities and transgressions so that we might have true peace and healing. When we face difficulties, we can trust the love and grace of Jesus and let His peace fill our souls.

Let us hand our worries and fears over to Jesus each day, believing that His redemption can bring true peace. Wherever we are and whatever we face, we can be full of confidence, because Jesus was punished for us and paid the price for our sins. Let us be firmly convinced that His love and compassion never end, and that He is the true source of our peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you deeply experience the peace and healing of Jesus every day. May you find strength in difficulty and pass on God’s love to others. Amen!

v: Grace to you and peace be multiplied in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord,
b: In this world each of us longs for peace, a true feeling of calm deep within. Yet we often find ourselves troubled by all kinds of disturbance and pressure and unable to truly experience this peace.
Today’s passage tells us that peace comes from knowing God and our Lord Jesus. When we build a close relationship with God and come to know Jesus, we can receive abundant grace and peace from Him.

Imagine a little child lost in a storm, frightened and bewildered. But when he sees his parents’ faces and hears their gentle voices, his heart immediately calms, because he knows he is under the shelter of love. In the same way, when we know God and build a close relationship with Him, we can feel His boundless love and comfort, and this brings us true peace.

A missionary went to a remote tribe to preach the gospel. The tribe was a place full of fear and discord, where people often hurt one another over fighting and possessions. But when the missionary told them the message of God’s love and peace, a wonderful change came over the tribe. People began to tolerate and understand one another, and they looked for peaceful ways to live together, because they had experienced the power of the true peace God gives.

In our own lives we may meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties that leave us lost and despairing. But when we truly know God and Jesus Christ, we can receive peace from Him, a peace that goes beyond anything the world can give.

Let us seek a close relationship with God every day and know Jesus Christ more deeply, so that in every circumstance we can experience His abundant grace and peace. May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you enjoy true peace on the journey of knowing God and Jesus Christ. Amen!

v: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;
b: In this world we are often influenced by many outside forces. These influences may come from social media, friends, family, or our own inner voice. When we let ourselves be ruled by the desires of the flesh, we often feel confused, empty, and without direction. But when we choose to set our minds on the Spirit and act according to His leading, we will gain life and peace. There was a sister named Jiarong. She had always longed to be a dancer, but her heart was often filled with self-doubt and fear.

Whenever she practiced her dance steps, the voice of the flesh told her she would never succeed and should give up. But whenever she quieted her heart and listened to the voice of the Holy Spirit, she felt strength and courage rise within her. The Holy Spirit told her that she was one of a kind and had talents given by God, and that if she believed, she could achieve her dream. Jiarong chose to set her mind on the Spirit, and with firm faith she studied and performed dance. In the end she became an outstanding dancer, bringing people endless joy and beauty.

This story tells us that when we choose to set our minds on the Spirit, everything in life becomes different. The Holy Spirit is the compass of our souls. He guides us onto the right path and brings us closer to God step by step. When we listen to the voice of the Holy Spirit and obey His leading, we will gain inner peace, and even outside difficulties and trials cannot shake our faith.

So let us choose, every day, to set our minds on the Spirit. When we feel lost or uneasy, let us rely on the strength of the Holy Spirit and return to the word of God. His word is the bread of our lives and gives us strength and wisdom to face challenges. Only through close communion with the Holy Spirit can we truly gain life and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you set your mind on the Spirit every day and every moment, and may you be satisfied and joyful in the life and peace He brings you. Amen!

v: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
b: In this passage Paul reminds us that God is a God of hope. When we believe in Him, He fills our hearts with joy and peace and, through the power of the Holy Spirit, gives us abundant hope.

Sometimes the difficulties and challenges in life can leave us discouraged and disappointed, but remember that God is the source of our hope. Like a ship in a storm, as long as we turn our faith to God, He will give peace so that even in hardship we keep our hope.
There was once a man who met a series of setbacks and failures in life and felt helpless and despairing. He lost his job and lost a loved one, and he felt he had fallen into a dark abyss.
Yet this man set out with a brave heart to find God’s hope. He began reading the Bible, looking in God’s word for comfort for his soul. During this time he met an old man, who told him a parable.

The old man said that there was a little tree battered by wind and rain, bent almost to the point of breaking. But no matter what, the tree kept on growing in the storm. In the end its trunk grew stronger and its branches and leaves grew more lush, and it became one of the most beautiful trees in the forest. The old man told the man that, like the tree, when we persevere through difficulties, God gives peace and hope and makes our lives more beautiful.

My friends, let us take this story as an example and face the challenges and difficulties of life bravely. Whatever difficulties we meet, as long as we believe in the hope of God, He will surely fill our hearts with joy and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. In every difficulty, may you find God’s hope and peace. May you abound in hope through the power of the Holy Spirit! Amen!

v: All your children will be taught by the LORD, and your children’s peace will be great.
b: In this passage God assures us that when our children are taught by God, they will have great peace. This brings us, as parents, great hope and confidence, because we know that if we entrust them to God, He will watch over them and guide them on the right path.

There was a mother named Xinhui who cared deeply about the growth of her son Xiaojie. Xiaojie met many difficulties at school and always felt discouraged and frustrated. Xinhui decided to pray to God, asking Him to give her wisdom and strength to teach Xiaojie.

One day, at a church gathering, Xinhui heard a parable about strawberries. The pastor said, “Life is like an orchard. Sometimes you will meet pests and drought, but if you hold on to faith and wait patiently, in the end you will taste delicious fruit.” This parable deeply touched Xinhui’s heart, and she knew that this was also God’s promise to her son Xiaojie.

Xinhui decided to teach this parable to Xiaojie and to explain that the difficulties and setbacks of life are only temporary, and that if he firmly believed God’s promise and waited patiently, he would taste true peace and joy. Xiaojie began to understand that he was not facing difficulty alone, but that he had a loving Heavenly Father walking with him and protecting him.

Time passed, and Xiaojie began to make progress in his studies, and his confidence grew day by day. Seeing her son’s growth, Xinhui was filled with comfort and gratitude, because she knew that all of this was God’s grace and help.

Dear family, in our lives we all face all kinds of difficulties and challenges. But when we believe God’s promise and entrust our children to Him, He will guide them on the right path and give them great peace.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your protection and teaching. Give us wisdom and strength to teach our children, so that they may obey Your will and walk on the right path. In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may your children all have great peace. Amen!
May the truth of this passage become part of our lives, and may we enjoy abundant peace in the light of faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your children all have great peace. Amen!

v: “Remember the word which Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, saying, ‘The LORD your God gives you rest, and will give you this land.
b: In this passage we see God, through Moses, convey an important message to the people of Israel: God would give them rest and give them the land. Peace is a gift God gives us. It goes beyond worldly stability and is an inner calm and comfort.

When we face the challenges of life, we often long for peace. But true peace is not a change in outward circumstances; it is experienced inwardly in our relationship with God. Just as Moses led the people of Israel through the wilderness, we too can rely on God’s guidance and find inner peace.

There was a little boy whose father was a fisherman. One day his father took him to the sea. The boy saw the vastness of the ocean and its surging waves and was very frightened. Seeing the fear on his face, his father said gently, “Son, as long as you hold my hand, however fierce the waves may be, you will be safe.”

This illustration tells us that when we walk with God, we can find true peace in difficulty and challenge. However great the storm we face, as long as we are with God, He will protect us, comfort us, and give us peace.

So let us seek a close relationship with God every day, ask for His guidance and protection, and believe that He will give us peace in our lives. When we face challenges, let us remember God’s promise and be firmly convinced that He will lead us through difficulty and give us peace in the end.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s peace and protection every day. May you walk with God on life’s journey and find true peace. Amen!

v: In his days, the righteous shall flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon is no more.
b: This passage tells us that in God’s Kingdom the righteous will have an abundant life, full of peace and blessing, like the bright moon.

There was a young man named Minglun who had dreamed since childhood of becoming a musician. He studied music diligently but often met setbacks and difficulties. Yet he never gave up and always firmly believed he had talent and potential. One day he received an opportunity to perform in a large concert, and he gave himself wholeheartedly, showing his unique talent and passion. As he played the beautiful notes, the hearts of the audience were moved and deeply inspired. Minglun’s music carried hope and peace, like the bright moon lighting up a dark night.

This story tells us that even when we face challenges and difficulties, as long as we believe in our own potential and hold on to faith, God will bring peace and blessing into our lives. The righteous walk with God and enjoy His grace and protection, like the bright moon bringing light into the night.

Perhaps you are in a low point of your life now, feeling lost and helpless. But let us remember this passage and let the hope and peace of the flourishing of the righteous fill our hearts. Whatever difficulties we face, as long as we keep our faith and believe in God’s promise, He will surely give us peace and success.

So let us hold on to the truth in this passage and believe that the righteous have peace, like the bright moon, lighting up our lives. When you face difficulties, may you hold on to your convictions and pursue your dreams with fresh courage and perseverance. May you become a person who gives off hope and peace and lights up yourself and those around you.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you stand firm in faith and live out the life of the righteous. Amen!

v: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side. There is no enemy and no evil occurrence.
b: This passage tells us that under God’s protection we can enjoy peace on every side, with no adversary and no calamity. This brings us comfort and reassurance, because we know our God is almighty and is our shield and refuge.

Imagine a little child who loses his way in a storm, frightened and in despair. But when he finds a large tree for shelter, he can find peace and safety under its cover. Just as this child found the tree, when we seek God and trust in Him, He becomes our refuge and protects us from the harm of adversaries and calamity.

In our lives we often meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we may feel helpless and lost. But remember that in all of this, God is the source of our peace. His love and compassion always surround us, and His arms protect us like a great tree, giving us strength and courage to face difficulties.
When we believe God’s word and rely on His strength, we need not fear any adversary or calamity. For we know that God’s peace, which surpasses all understanding, can settle in our hearts.

So let us lay down all our worries and fears and entrust our faith fully to the God who gives us peace on every side. Whatever difficulty we face, He will surely be at our side, giving us strength and wisdom.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s peace every day, and in every circumstance deeply feel His love and protection. Amen!

v: All Judah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found by them. Then the LORD gave them rest all around.
b: In this passage we see that the people of Judah, by seeking God with all their heart, brought about joy and peace. They did not merely speak an oath carelessly, but sought Yahweh sincerely and with all their heart. This firm and sincere attitude received God’s promise and blessing, and the result was peace on every border. So when we seek God with all our heart, make a covenant with Him, and keep that covenant firmly, we can receive God’s blessing and have peace in every area.

Imagine a man standing before a great mountain. He sees sparse patches of grass on it, and these small tufts are like our difficulties and challenges, whether in study, work, relationships, or other areas.

This man decided to climb the mountain, and so he began his journey. At first he found it very hard, but he did not retreat. He climbed step by step, passing through many difficult stages, and both his body and his spirit were tested.

Yet he kept looking up toward the sunlight on the mountain, and this gave him hope and courage. He told himself, “I believe I can climb to the top, because God is with me, and He will give me strength and peace.” Every step was upheld by faith, hope, and love, and he kept on going.

At last, when he reached the summit, he was rewarded with a beautiful view, with wide vistas all around, as if all the troubles of the world had become insignificant. He felt boundless peace, because he knew he had overcome all the challenges and difficulties.

Friends, this parable tells us that when we seek God with all our heart and rely on His strength to face the difficulties and challenges of life, we too can experience peace on every border. The peace God gives us surpasses human understanding. It does not come because our circumstances have improved, but because we walk with God and believe He will watch over us in every situation.

So let us firmly build our relationship with God, seek Him with all our heart, and believe that He will give us peace and lead us over every mountain peak in our lives. However great the problem we face, as long as we walk with God, we can overcome everything.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find peace and strength in your relationship with God, and whatever difficulty you face, may you be able to rely on God’s promise and guidance. Amen!

v: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.
b: In Proverbs chapter 3, verse 17, we see a beautiful truth: the path of God's wisdom is full of pleasantness and peace. This verse reminds us that when we follow God's way, He will give us peace and joy.

We live in a world full of challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we seem to lose our way and feel lost and helpless. But when we trust God and follow His path, He will lead us onto the road of peace.

There was a young man named Zhongren. On life's journey he met with many hardships and setbacks, and he felt lost and discouraged. But he decided to look for God's way and to trust His guidance. He began to read the Bible, to pray, and to join a church.

As time went by, Zhongren discovered that his life had become more meaningful and peaceful. He learned to forgive others and to treat the people around him with love and care. He built deep relationships with his family and friends, and he found success in his work. Though difficulties still came, he knew that God's way had brought him true peace.

This story tells us that when we choose to follow God's way, He will lead us onto the road of peace. That road may not be the easiest, but on it we will find true comfort and joy. We can learn to treat others with love, to let go of the wounds of the past, and to hold on to faith and hope.

So let us choose every day to walk in God's way, facing life's challenges with faith and hope. Let us support and encourage one another, and look for opportunities each day to live out the peace and joy God gives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience true peace and joy as you walk in God's way. Amen!

v: My people will live in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places,
b: In this busy and ever-changing world, we all long to find a peaceful habitation, a place where our hearts can find calm and comfort. This verse tells us that God wants to give us such peace, so that even in hardship and challenge we can find a safe dwelling.

A traveler wandered over mountains and rivers, looking for a place to rest. After a long journey, he finally came upon a beautiful lake, and beside the lake stood a quiet, cozy little house. He went in and felt a stillness far from the noise of the world. Here he found a true resting place.

This story tells us that, just as the traveler found a peaceful home, we too can find true peace in God's love. When we entrust ourselves to God and believe in His protection and provision, we can find inner calm in the midst of life's clamor.

In real life we also often meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we may feel lost and helpless, but when we remember the truth of this verse, we can keep our faith. Just as the traveler only needed to find a quiet lake, we only need to turn our eyes to God and seek His guidance, and we will find our own peaceful dwelling even in hard times.

So today, let us not panic over the challenges of life, but trust God's promise, knowing that He will give us a peaceful habitation. Let us hand over all our troubles and worries to Him, and let Him be our true place of safety.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you find a peaceful habitation in this world, and a safe dwelling under God's protection. May your heart be at rest, and may you face life's challenges with faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.
b: In this passage, God reminds us to pray for kings and all who are in authority, so that we may spend each day in godliness, dignity, and peace. This is not only a requirement for the believers of that time, but also a guide for our own lives.

There was a young man named Mark who had set his heart from childhood on becoming a doctor. But the world does not always go the way we plan. Just as Mark was preparing to apply to medical school, he was suddenly diagnosed with an illness that was very hard to cure.
Faced with this blow, Mark felt despair and confusion; he did not know how to face the shattering of his dream. Yet Mark did not give up. He decided to pursue his dream in another way.

Mark gathered his courage and became a medical volunteer. With his limited strength and time, he went to help people in need. Although he could not become a real doctor, he still cared for the health of others with love and compassion.

This story tells us that a tranquil life does not mean having no difficulties or challenges. But like Mark, we can meet adversity with the right attitude and faith. We can give our abilities and our love to others, and even if we cannot realize our original dream, we can still find our own accomplishment in a tranquil and quiet life.

Let us take the truth of this passage as our foundation and bless our families and communities. May they live in godliness, dignity, and peace; may they overcome difficulties and care for the needs of others with love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find your own accomplishment in a tranquil life, and may you help others with love and compassion. Amen!

t: Peace to All That You Have
v: Tell him, ‘Long life to you! Peace be to you! Peace be to your house! Peace be to all that you have!
b: In this passage we see David blessing a wealthy man's household and all that he had with the peace of God. This is more than a word of greeting; it shows God's care and concern for every part of our lives. In life we often chase success and wealth, hoping they will bring peace and happiness. Yet true peace does not depend on our wealth or position; it comes from inner calm and trust in God.

There was once a young man named Tom, who came from a poor family but always dreamed of becoming a successful entrepreneur. He worked hard, kept learning and growing, and achieved great success in his career. But he found that as his wealth increased, his heart had no real peace or contentment.

One day Tom met a Christian of firm faith, who shared his belief and the true source of peace. This person told Tom that peace is not found in the pursuit of material wealth, but is gained in the process of building an intimate relationship with God.

Tom began to seek true peace. He started reading the Bible, praying, attending church gatherings, and built a deep relationship with God. That relationship gave him inner peace, and whatever difficulties and challenges he met in life, he could face them with faith.

In the same way, each of us can be inspired by this story. Whatever our circumstances, true peace is found only in our relationship with God. When we build an intimate connection with Him, He will give us calm and quiet in our hearts, so that we can face every challenge in life.
Let us walk with God every day and seek true peace. Peace to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that you have.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find peace and joy as you seek God's way. Amen!

v: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
b: In this passage we see God promising perfect peace to those who trust in Him with a steadfast mind. How wonderful and exciting! When we fully believe in, depend on, and rely on God, He will surely protect us and let us feel perfect peace in our lives.

There was a boy named Zhelun. Xiaoming had carried an important dream since he was little: he wanted to be a gardener, creating beautiful gardens that would bring people joy and calm. But his family and friends all laughed at him, thinking it was an impossible dream.

Despite hardships and setbacks, Zhelun never gave up his faith in his dream. Every morning when he got up, he prayed to God and relied on His power and guidance. This firm conviction gave Zhelun the strength and courage to pursue his dream.

One spring morning, Xiaoming finally realized his dream. He succeeded in creating a beautiful garden, full of colorful flowers and green leaves. People came to the garden and felt a wonderful calm and comfort; their hearts were healed and gladdened.

This story tells us that when we trust steadfastly in God, He will protect us and give us perfect peace. Like Zhelun, we too may face pressure, setbacks, and voices of distrust. But when we persist in believing and relying on God's power, we will experience the peace and protection He has promised.

So in our daily lives, let us keep holding on to faith, hope, and love, and whatever difficulties or challenges come, trust confidently in God. He will surely give us perfect peace and lead us toward a bright future.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you steadfastly rely on God every day and experience the perfect peace He gives. Amen!

v: The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
b: This passage tells us that when we pursue righteousness, we will receive peace and stability.

In our lives there are many times when we may meet difficulty, pressure, and unfairness. But when we choose to walk the path of righteousness, God will surely give us peace and stability. Like a tree rooted in rich soil, receiving sunshine and rain every day, it grows strong, its branches flourish, and it bears beautiful fruit. In the same way, when we make righteousness our foundation, act justly in daily life, and show kindness and love to others, we will see the fruit of peace that God gives.

There was a man named Lot who ran a small restaurant in a small town. Though business was not good, Lot always insisted on using the best ingredients, and he treated his customers with love and diligence. One day a traveler passed through the town, heard of the small restaurant's good food and service, and decided to try it. After eating there, he was moved by Lot's warmth and the delicious food, so he recommended the restaurant to his friends and shared his experience on social media. Many people came to eat there, and Lot's business grew more and more prosperous.

This story tells us that when we pour righteousness and love into our work and lives, we will gain abundant fruit. It not only brings blessing to others, but also lets us feel peace and stability ourselves. Like Lot's restaurant in the small town, people will be moved by our actions and attitudes, and will share their joy and blessings with us.

So let us, every day, choose to face the challenges and difficulties of life with righteousness and love. Let us walk with others and treat them with kindness and care. When we do so, we will taste the fruit of peace and stability that God gives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May we all find peace and stability on the path of pursuing righteousness. Amen!

v: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
b: This passage reminds us that on life's journey we sometimes go through pain and hardship, and even feel lost and in despair. But when we accept God's discipline and shaping through these experiences, we will find that behind the suffering the fruit of peace is growing, which is God's righteousness fulfilling His purpose.

It is like a seed planted in the soil: it needs water, sunlight, and nutrients to grow strong. But for the seed to grow, the farmer must watch the seasons and the weather, sometimes giving enough water and sometimes a little less, to suit different conditions. In this process the seed may meet some difficulties and challenges, but only when it finally grows into a fruitful plant can we see the wisdom and love of the farmer.

Life is the same. Some of the things that happen to us are tests and lessons designed by God. These difficulties may make us feel pain and distress, but it is through these experiences that our faith and perseverance grow. When we learn to obey God's will and accept His discipline of our lives, we can see the fruit of peace beginning to grow behind the suffering. It is also like a stonemason making a beautiful statue: with hammer and chisel he shapes the stone bit by bit until it becomes a work of art. This process takes patience and perseverance, and the mason must face pain and toil. Yet he knows that only through such effort can an ordinary stone become a stunning work of art.

In the same way, as we are polished by life's difficulties and trials, we also need to keep patience and perseverance. We must believe that these challenges are meant to help us grow and to experience greater blessing. God is our stonemason; He is carving our lives, making us His workmanship, to display His glory.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep your faith when you face difficulties and trials in life, believing that God's plan is far beyond our imagination, and may you learn obedience and growth through these experiences. May you bear the fruit of peace in every challenge, and reveal the glory of God. Amen!

v: For you shall go out with joy, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.
b: In this passage God assures us of peace and guidance. When we walk with God, He will lead us in the way of righteousness and peace. Just as the mountains and hills sing and the trees of the field clap their hands, all of nature welcomes and blesses us.

In our lives we may sometimes go through hardship or challenge. But let us not lose faith, because God has promised us peace and guidance. It is like a traveler lost in a vast desert who, on seeing a tall tree, knows he has found the right way. That tree is God's guidance; He always shows us the way to peace.

There was a girl named Sally. She lived in poverty and had to work hard every day to support herself and her family. Although she faced many difficulties, she never gave up her faith and hope in life.

One day on her way home, Sally met an old man. The old man told her about a new path, which would lead her to a land of plenty and change her life. Sally thanked the old man and decided to take the path.

Sally set out toward her new goal. Though the road was hard, she believed what the old man had said. As she passed through a barren land, she saw a tall tree. The tree stood for hope and guidance, and let her know she was on the right road. Sally kept going, and in the end she arrived at a beautiful and fertile place, and her life was changed from then on.

This story tells us that when we face difficulties and challenges, we must not lose heart. Instead, we should keep our faith and keep going under God's guidance. Wherever we are, as long as we hold to the principles of righteousness and peace, God will surely lead us to the land of peace that is ours.
So, dear family, let us believe God's promise and keep faith and hope in hard times. He will surely lead us, so that we can be led out in peace
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience the grace of peace and guidance in your life, just as the mountains and hills sing and the trees of the field clap their hands. May you find the right path when you are lost, and experience change and abundance in your life. Amen!

v: to shine on those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death; to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
b: These are the words of Luke chapter 1, verse 79. When we feel despair and helplessness in the dark, God's word reminds us that He will guide our feet into the way of peace.

On the journey of life we may meet all kinds of difficulties and challenges. Sometimes we may fall into darkness and feel lonely and hopeless. Yet this verse tells us that even in the darkest moments, we can still shine light for those who sit in darkness. We can become a lamp of hope, bringing them light and peace.

There was a man named Dechang who met many difficulties and challenges in life. He lost his job and faced financial pressure, and he felt despair and helplessness. But Dechang did not give up; he decided to look for the way of peace.

Dechang spent a long time thinking and reflecting, and he began to look for ways to solve his problems. He learned some new skills and began to help people in need in his community. Every day he used his actions to shine light on those who sat in darkness, bringing them hope and peace.

In the end Dechang found a new job and regained the confidence he had lost. His life became full of peace and hope. This story tells us that even in hardship we can look for the way of peace. By helping others and becoming a lamp of light, we can bring them hope and peace.

So let each of us become a light for those in darkness. Let us use our love and care to bring them peace and hope. Whatever challenges we meet in life, let us remember God's word: He will guide our feet into the way of peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel the guidance of peace and hope at every step. Amen!

v: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
b: In this passage we see a woman who came to Jesus full of faith to be healed of her illness. She had gone through much hardship and frustration, but she believed that if she could only touch Jesus, she would be healed. The words Jesus spoke to her healed not only her body, but also the pain and despair in her heart.

This passage reveals an important truth to us: the power of faith. When we face the troubles and challenges of life with firm faith, God's grace and power come upon us. Like this woman, she was healed and given peace because of her faith, and she could go home in peace.

In our lives we also often meet all kinds of troubles and setbacks. Sometimes we may feel helpless and desperate, not knowing how to face these difficulties. But it is exactly at such times that we need to be like this woman, keeping firm faith and believing in God's power and promises.

Perhaps some are facing a health challenge, and illness keeps you from living normally. Perhaps some are going through emotional pain, having lost a loved one or suffered betrayal and hurt. Whatever the trouble, we can believe that as long as we hold on to faith and seek God's help, He will surely give us healing and peace.

We can learn from this woman's testimony. She was healed not only because of faith, but also received peace because of faith. Her faith changed not only her own life, but also became an example for us. When we respond to trouble with a peaceful heart and trust God's will and plan, we will find His grace and power shown in our lives.

So today, let us take courage. Whether we face physical challenges or other difficulties, let us call on God's help with firm faith. Believe that He will give us healing and peace, so that we can return in peace to our families and workplaces.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive peace and healing through faith, and may you share God's love and hope with those around you. Amen!

v: Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
b: In this passage God calls us to obey His commandments, and He promises that we will receive peace and righteousness as abundant as rivers and the waves of the sea. What a wonderful promise!

Yet in real life we often face all kinds of difficulties and challenges that make us lose our sense of peace and righteousness. Sometimes we may experience pressure at work, friction in relationships, or trouble with health and finances. These difficulties leave us confused and helpless, and we lose our sense of direction for peace.

But let us remember that God's promise is eternal and is not affected by our circumstances. Just as a river never stops flowing and the waves never stop rising and falling, God's peace and righteousness exist forever. When we obey God's commandments and entrust our difficulties to Him, we can experience this flow of peace and righteousness.

There was a Christian named Alex who lost his job and his family in an accident. He felt despair and helplessness, yet he held firmly to God's promise. He decided to stop and listen quietly for God's guidance.

As Alex sought God, he realized that he had always been chasing his own goals, without putting God's will first. He began to change his way of life, devoting more time and energy to serving others and sharing God's love and care.
This change brought inner peace to Alex, and also brought change to the people around him. He saw his family and friends begin to seek the truth and experience God's miracles.

This story reminds us that when we face difficulties and challenges, we must not give up seeking God's guidance. When we obey His commandments and put Him first, we will experience peace flowing like a river and righteousness surging like the waves of the sea.

So let us strengthen our faith, rely on God's power, entrust our difficulties to Him, and act according to His will. When we do so, we will experience peace flowing like a river and righteousness overflowing like the waves of the sea.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's peace and righteousness on this journey. May your life flow like a river, bringing God's grace and lovingkindness to everyone you meet. Amen!

v: But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
b: In this passage God tells us that the humble will inherit the land and delight in abundant peace. This passage reminds us that choosing humility rather than pride will bring us true peace and joy.

There is a story about a humble farmer who worked hard every day to cultivate his land and entrusted everything he had to God. He was not only a hardworking farmer, but also a cheerful and steadfast Christian. Whenever he met difficulties and setbacks, he always believed with full confidence that God would provide for him.

One year he planted a field, but the weather was dry and the crops could not grow. Many people began to worry that their crops would wither and life would become hard. Yet this farmer remained humble and full of faith, believing that God would give him abundant peace.

Just when people were giving up hope, a heavy rain suddenly fell, bringing life-giving water to the whole region. The humble farmer's field turned green, the crops grew strong, and the harvest was rich. His neighbors were amazed and asked how he had done it. He answered humbly that it was God's grace and blessing, the result of his delighting in peace.

This story tells us that when we choose humility and believe in God's promises, we will inherit abundant blessing and peace. Even when we face difficulties and setbacks, as long as we keep faith and humility, God will prepare for us.
So let us delight in peace every day, humbly trusting God's guidance and provision. However great the difficulty we face, we can rest assured that God will prepare an abundant future for us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you delight in peace every day, and humbly trust in God's grace and blessing. Amen!

v: Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
b: This passage reminds us that where lovingkindness and truth meet, and righteousness and peace kiss each other, God's kingdom is there. It is a beautiful experience, one that fills our hearts with peace and harmony.

In our lives we sometimes meet all kinds of challenges and conflicts. We may feel confused, doubtful, or anxious. But when we face these troubles with lovingkindness and honesty, we will find that God's peace meets us, giving us strength and hope. There was once a woman named Xinhua, who was always full of love and care and often helped those in need. She believed that through lovingkindness and goodwill she could change the world.

One day, as she was walking on the street, she met a homeless old woman. The old woman looked exhausted, with no money and nowhere to go. Xinhua immediately felt God's calling; she stopped and talked with the old woman, and gave her some food and warm clothing.
This story tells us that when lovingkindness meets truth, miracles happen. Xinhua's good deed not only gave herself peace, but also brought peace and joy to the homeless old woman.
In the same way, righteousness and peace also need to come together. We live in a world full of unfairness and strife, and as the Psalm says, we need to let righteousness and peace meet.

There was a young man named Derui, who was passionate about justice and firmly believed that everyone should be treated fairly. In a social organization he fought hard for the rights of the poor, and worked with the government to improve the environment of the community.

This story tells us that when righteousness and peace meet, hope and harmony spring up. Derui's efforts made the community fairer and more prosperous, and everything he did brought people peace and hope.

Let us think about how we can let lovingkindness, truth, righteousness, and peace come together in our lives. When we treat others with lovingkindness, we can build sincere relationships. When we pursue righteousness, we can bring harmony and peace.

May we become people who hold lovingkindness and truth, righteousness and peace together. Let us show God's love and miracles through our actions and attitudes. May God's lovingkindness and truth meet us, and make us a force that changes the world.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you be blessed as you pursue righteousness and peace. Amen!

t: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem
v: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem. Those who love you will prosper.
b: In this passage God calls us to pray for peace in Jerusalem, but we can also extend this idea to our own lives. Each of us has our own “Jerusalem,” the city of our heart, which represents our inner peace and happiness.

Life often brings difficulties and challenges, just as Jerusalem once faced war and destruction. Yet we can draw strength and wisdom from the history of Jerusalem. Just as those who love Jerusalem will prosper, when we treat ourselves and others with love, our hearts will also prosper.

In this process we may need to build walls that protect our hearts, like the walls of Jerusalem. These walls can be healthy habits of life, such as good sleep, a balanced diet, and regular exercise. They can also be cultivating positive thoughts and attitudes, such as gratitude and forgiveness.

We can also learn from those who love Jerusalem how to face adversity with a peaceful spirit. Life is full of pressure and conflict, but if we respond with a calm mind, we can keep the peace in our hearts.

Let us remember that whatever we face in life, we can ask God to give us peace. When we pray to Him and seek His guidance and shelter, He will surely answer our cry. Just as Jerusalem received God's protection, we too can find peace and happiness under God's great love and grace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. As you journey in pursuit of peace of heart, whatever difficulties you meet, may you receive strength and courage from the Lord. May your heart prosper, and may peace fill your life. Amen!

v: and to give relief to you who are afflicted with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels in flaming fire,
b: Life is often full of afflictions and trials, and sometimes we may feel weary and alone, but let us remember that we are not fighting alone. God promises that we will receive peace together, and He sends His angels with His power to help us. There was a young man named Danny, who came from a poor family. After his parents died, he was forced to face life's hardships alone. Yet he was full of faith and hope, believing that God would lead him out of his difficulties.

Danny studied hard, and in order to go to university he took many jobs to earn tuition. Though it was hard, he never gave up. In the end he succeeded in entering a famous university and began the journey of his dream.

At university Danny met some setbacks and difficulties, but he always kept a peaceful heart. He often prayed, entrusting his worries to God, and believed that God would help him when he needed it most.

After graduating, Danny chose a job that did not pay well but was full of a sense of mission. He went to a poor region to help people in need. He gave them not only material help but also faith and hope, letting them know they were not alone, and that God was with them.
As today's passage says, God will surely give those of us who are afflicted peace together. Whatever trouble or challenge we face, let us remember God's promise and trust His power and help.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel God's peace in every difficulty and triumph in His strength. Amen!

v: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”
b: In life we may face suffering and challenges. Sometimes pressure and hardship leave us at a loss, as if trapped in darkness. Yet when we believe in Jesus Christ and walk with Him, we can find peace in adversity.

Our lives are like a journey full of twists and challenges. On this journey we sometimes meet rugged mountain roads, and sometimes bumpy rivers. But when we rely firmly on the Lord, He will lead us at our side, and give us peace and strength. There was a young man who met with many setbacks and difficulties in life and felt very desperate. One day he met an old man who looked very peaceful and kind. He asked the old man, “Why do you look so calm and happy? I have always hoped to have a heart like that.”

The old man smiled and answered, “My child, peace is not the absence of difficulty and pain; it is being able to trust God and believe His promises when we face difficulty. We can hand our troubles and worries over to Him, because He has overcome the world.” The old man's words deeply touched the young man's heart.

From this story we can also understand that peace does not come from outward circumstances, but from our trust in and reliance on God. When we hand our difficulties and worries over to God, we can find true peace and hope in Him. In the Bible there is a story that moved me deeply. It is about Paul, an apostle of the Lord, who was imprisoned. Although he was in difficult circumstances, he never lost his faith. In the dark prison he sang praises to God, and in prayer he received peace and strength. This story tells us that even in the hardest times we can still have peace, as long as we believe God's promises and rely on His power.

So, my dear family, whatever suffering and challenges you face right now, please remember these words in the Bible: “In me you may have peace. In the world you have oppression; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.” Believe in Jesus Christ and rely on His promises and power, and no matter what, we will find peace and hope in difficulty.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive the peace and strength God gives in every challenge. Amen!

v: Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding joy. I will praise you on the harp, God, my God.
b: In this passage the psalmist expresses how he went to God's altar and found God, his exceeding joy. This passage reminds us that when we feel joy, excitement, or gratitude, we should not forget to come before God and praise Him.

In our lives we are sometimes happy and glad because of all kinds of things. Perhaps it is good news, a job that makes us glad, or a wonderful relationship. And when this joy rises in our hearts, we should learn from the psalmist to come before God with thankful and praising hearts.

There was a man named Zhiguang who met many challenges and difficulties in life. But even in adversity he was always able to keep a joyful heart. This was because Zhiguang believed that every challenge was a chance for growth given to him by God.

Once, Zhiguang faced a huge challenge at work. He was forced to take on a very heavy task, and the time was very tight. But Zhiguang did not lose heart or despair; instead, he chose to see this difficulty as an opportunity, a chance to show his abilities.

In the course of completing the task, Zhiguang was not only full of energy and creativity, but also experienced God's help and guidance. In the end he completed the task successfully and received praise and recognition. Zhiguang knew that all this came as a blessing from the God who is his exceeding joy.

This story tells us that when we face challenges, we can choose to meet them with a joyful spirit, and believe that God will give us strength and wisdom to overcome difficulties. Like the psalmist, we can come before God and praise Him on the harp, because He is our exceeding joy.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You that You are our exceeding joy. Grant us joyful hearts, so that even in difficulties and challenges we may face them with thanksgiving and praise.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's joy and peace every day. Amen!

v: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and will lift up your face to God.
b: In life we are often tested by all kinds of challenges and difficulties, which may leave us discouraged and disappointed, and even make us lose faith. Yet God teaches us to delight in the Almighty and to lift up our faces to God. This means that we should place our joy and hope on God's power and promises.

A young athlete took part in an important competition, full of confidence and hope in his performance. But in the competition he met many challenges and difficulties, and felt very discouraged and disappointed. Yet he decided not to give up. He remembered God's word, and began to delight in the Almighty and to lift up his face to God. He believed that God would help him overcome difficulties and achieve his goal.

In the end, this young athlete won the competition with an amazing performance, and his joy and gratitude were beyond words. He understood that it was because he had placed his joy in the Almighty and trusted God's help that he was able to overcome difficulties and win.

In our lives, too, we may meet all kinds of difficulties and challenges, and we may feel disappointed and helpless. But when we choose to delight in the Almighty and lift up our faces to God, we will find that God's strength and help are limitless. Whatever our situation, as long as we believe in God's power and promises, we can go forward with confidence.

Listening to this verse today, we are reminded not to focus only on our own troubles and challenges, but to place our joy and hope on the Almighty. When we face difficulties, let us delight in the Almighty and believe in God's power and promises, and this will bring us faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you always delight in the Almighty on life's way, and lift up your face to God. Amen!

v: You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in the LORD. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
b: In this passage we can see a very interesting image: troublesome things are winnowed like chaff into the air and scattered by the wind. This picture gives us a feeling of joy, just as when we hand over our worries, fears, and difficulties to God, He gently blows them away and lets us feel free from care.

In life we often face all kinds of challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we may feel heavy pressure, or even helpless and desperate. But as this passage says, we should rejoice in Yahweh and glory in Him. When we put our faith in God and believe in His power and promises, we will find that joy and peace well up from within.

We can imagine a person standing on a beach, facing the magnificent ocean. He looks at the vast sea, feels the sea breeze brush his cheeks, and listens to the sound of the waves. All this fills him with joy and calm. In the same way, when we turn our eyes to God and rejoice and glory in Him, we will experience spiritual abundance and peace, just like the man standing on the beach.

It is also like a gardener who spent much time and effort planting a tree. He nurtured it, watered it, and protected it, and finally saw it grow strong. When the tree was in flower and fruit, the gardener felt great joy and pride. In the same way, when we entrust our lives to God and let Him guide and nurture us, we will see miracles blossom in our lives. This will bring us great joy and satisfaction.

So let us rejoice in Yahweh every day and glory in Him. Whatever difficulties we face, let us trust His love, faithfulness, and power. When we hand our worries and difficulties over to Him, He will help us blow them away, and bring us faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's grace and guidance on your journey of seeking joy. Amen!

v: Indeed your statutes are my delight, and my counselors.
b: When we read this verse, we can feel that the psalmist is full of joy in God's testimonies and relies on them. He regards God's testimonies as his counselors, which means that he takes God's word as the guidance and help for his life. This joyful attitude is admirable and worth learning from.

In our daily lives we may sometimes feel confused or helpless, not knowing what is right to do. But when we pursue God's testimonies, His word, with a joyful heart, we will find a marvelous power in them.
Many years ago there was a young man named Rongchang, who met a series of setbacks at work, and his dream became dim. Peter felt lost, not knowing which way to go.

One day he sought God's guidance and began to study the Bible. He found Psalm 119:24, which says that God's testimonies are my delight. A thought struck him, and he decided to treat God's word as the counselor of his life.

In the days that followed, Rongchang worked hard to keep God's word and applied it to his work and life. He learned patience and kindness, and kept a joyful attitude in the face of difficulties. This change brought back his passion for work and for life.
In the end, Rongchang made a breakthrough in his work and became a successful entrepreneur. His story has inspired many people, because it shows how joy and God's word can change a person's life.

Let us learn from Rongchang's story: by joyfully keeping God's testimonies, we too can find direction and abundance in life. When we walk in God's way with a joyful heart, we will find that His word has become our most reliable counselor.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find joy and peace as you pursue God's testimonies. May your life be filled with goodness through faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: Direct me in the path of your commandments, for I delight in them.
b: In this verse we see a very important idea: delighting in the Lord's commands. When we keep God's commands, we can gain joy and satisfaction from them.

There was a young man named Haoyu, who studied very hard in the hope of getting into his ideal university. He spent a great deal of time in front of his books and gave up many chances for entertainment and rest. Although he faced many difficulties and pressures in his studies, he persevered, because he knew that only in this way could he realize his dream.

Delighting in keeping the Lord's commands is like Haoyu's effort. When we keep God's commands and face the difficulties and challenges of life, we may feel pressure, but we must persevere, because we know this is our goal, and through this path we can gain true joy and satisfaction.

It is like a farmer who works in the field, plowing, irrigating, and waiting patiently, until at last we see the seeds sprout, grow, and bear abundant fruit. This is because the farmer followed the laws of nature and enjoys the joy of harvest.
In the same way, when we keep God's commands and wait patiently like the farmer, we will see God's grace and blessing begin to sprout and grow in our lives and bear abundant fruit.

Let us now bring this truth into our lives. Whatever difficulties and challenges we face, let us persevere in keeping God's commands, because this is where our joy lies. Let us pursue our goals diligently like Haoyu, and wait patiently like the farmer for the harvest of God's grace and blessing.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true joy and satisfaction in keeping God's commands. Amen!

v: for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
b: In this passage we see that what God's kingdom values is not merely material enjoyment, but rather the righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit that we experience. This tells us that true joy comes from building a relationship with God, doing His will, and having inner peace.

We can understand this truth through an illustration from daily life. Suppose you are traveling to a destination, the scenery along the way is beautiful, and the restaurants and cafes are enticing. But if you focus only on eating, drinking, and having fun, and neglect your true destination, you may miss a greater blessing. In the same way, though material enjoyment is good, we must not make it the only goal we pursue. We should take righteousness and peace as our foundation, and look for true joy in the Holy Spirit.

Let us think about how to experience this joy in daily life. When we act with justice and integrity, whether at work or in our dealings with others, we can bring joy. When we pursue peaceful and harmonious relationships, and are willing to forgive and bear with others, we can feel joy in our hearts. When we draw near to the Holy Spirit and obey God's will, the Holy Spirit gives us supernatural joy, and whatever the outward circumstances, we can keep peace in our hearts.

So let us turn our attention from pure material enjoyment to what is more important. Let us press forward in pursuing righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. In this way we will find that, in a deep relationship with God, true joy will fill our souls.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you experience joy in the Holy Spirit on your journey of pursuing righteousness and peace, and may you feel God's endless blessing every day. Amen!

v: You became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit,
b: In our lives, meeting difficulties and challenges is unavoidable. We may meet unemployment, a broken heart, physical suffering, or other kinds of trouble. But this passage tells us that in great affliction we can receive the joy given by the Holy Spirit.

Imagine a man sailing at sea who is suddenly struck by a storm and huge waves, yet he is not afraid. Instead, he stands joyfully on the deck, because he knows there is a captain at the helm, and he believes the captain can bring him safely through the storm. It is because he trusts the captain that he can keep his joy in the midst of this difficulty.

In our lives this captain is our Lord Jesus Christ. When we believe in Him and rely on Him, the joy He gives us will rise above any difficulty. This joy is not based on a change in outward circumstances, but comes from inner faith, hope, and love.

In a small village there was a young man named Changan. Changan had lived in poverty since he was little, and his family often could not make ends meet. Yet although he was in hardship, Peter always lived with joy.

Changan's joy came from his faith in God. He believed God's promises, and believed that God would supply his needs. Every day he prayed to God and thanked Him for every small grace He gave, even a simple meal or a warm bed. Changan knew that even in great affliction, God's joy was still there.

My dear family, let us follow Changan's example. Though we may face difficulties, let us trust God's word and His promises to us. When we meet difficulties with faith and hope, the Holy Spirit will give us spiritual joy, and this joy will let us stand firm in adversity.

In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive in great affliction the joy given by the Holy Spirit, may God's word become the guide of your life, and may you follow the example of the Lord Jesus Christ. May you be filled with the strength of joy in every difficulty, and may your faith, hope, and love never be extinguished. Amen!

v: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
b: In every day of our lives there are many things that bring us frustration and difficulty. But when our lives are filled with the fruit of the Spirit, we will experience the joy God brings us.

There was a young man named Rongen who worked as a nurse in a hospital. Every day he faced all kinds of illness and suffering, but he always worked with a joyful smile. One day a patient asked him, “How do you manage to stay so joyful?”

Rongen answered, “Each of us will face difficulty and pain, but I believe God will give us strength and joy. Every day I spend time in fellowship with God, letting the fruit of the Spirit bear abundant joy in my heart. This joy enables me to face difficulties, and also to bring comfort and hope to patients and colleagues.”
As Rongen said, when we draw near to God and cultivate the fruit of the Spirit, we can find true joy in life. This is not worldly happiness, but joy based on faith and hope.

We can cultivate the fruit of joy in several ways. First, we should keep a heart of gratitude at all times. Whatever difficulty we face, we should remember God's grace and all that He has given us. Second, we should learn to let go of past mistakes and grudges, and respond to others with love. Finally, we should seek communion with the Holy Spirit, and let His joy fill our hearts.
Dear family, may we cultivate the fruit of joy of the Holy Spirit every day, and let this joy become our perseverance and strength in difficulties.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you have true joy every day! Amen!

v: Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and gladness are in his place.
b: This passage reminds us that when we enter God's sanctuary, we can experience honor, majesty, strength, and joy. So what is God's sanctuary?

In the Bible, many places are called God's sanctuary, such as the temple and the church. But more importantly, our own hearts can also become God's sanctuary. When we give our hearts completely to God, He will fill our lives and bring honor, majesty, strength, and joy.

There was a young man named Hecheng, who was often bullied by his classmates at school, which left him feeling inferior and helpless. He was always mocked and excluded, and felt discouraged and powerless. But his life began to change when he decided to hand his troubles over to God.

Hecheng began to enter God's sanctuary, which was his prayer room. He poured out to God all his wounds and challenges. He learned to trust God, and to believe that His honor and majesty were before him.

Before long, Hecheng began to see God's power at work in him. He made a breakthrough in his studies and became a top student in his class. His classmates began to respect him and seek his help. Joy and strength filled Hecheng's life, and he became a truly inspiring testimony.

This story inspires us: when we meet difficulties and challenges, we should not forget to enter God's sanctuary. In prayer we can give ourselves fully to Him and believe in His honor and majesty. When we trust Him, His strength and joy will fill our lives.
So, dear family, I
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. May you, when you face difficulties, be able to enter God's sanctuary, believe in His honor and majesty, and experience His strength and joy. Amen!

t: Joy in the House of Prayer
v: I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”
b: In this passage God shows us His love and compassion for us. He assures us that when we come to His house to pray, He will bring us to His holy mountain and make us joyful there. It is a promise full of hope and joy.
In life we often face all kinds of challenges and hardships. Sometimes we may feel helpless and desperate, but by believing God's promises we can find strength and a spring of joy in them.

Like a traveler who, after a long and arduous journey, finally arrives at his destination, when we meet God in prayer we also feel the same delight and comfort. It is a deep joy, a joy that goes beyond material pleasure, a joy that belongs to the soul.

We can apply this passage to our lives. When we face challenges and difficulties, let us not forget to come to God's house and seek His strength and wisdom. Prayer is the channel that connects us with God, and through prayer we can receive spiritual joy and peace.

In prayer we are like a seed, slowly growing strong until it bears beautiful flowers and fruit. This is God's work in us; in our hearts He is cultivating the character of love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, and goodness.

So today we can come with full confidence to God's house, to pray and seek His face. Let us believe that when we pray with thankful and joyful hearts, God will accept our burnt offerings and sacrifices. His house will become the place where we meet Him and seek strength.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find joy and peace in prayer, and receive strength and wisdom from God's house. Amen!

v: Always rejoice. Pray without ceasing. In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
b: Joy is God's will, and that is an uplifting message. When we meet difficulties and challenges, rejoicing always does not seem an easy thing. But this passage reminds us that joy is the will God has set for us, and He hopes that we can rejoice at all times.

There was a Christian full of faith, hope, and love named Xiaoling. She was an ordinary but steadfast believer who faced life's challenges every day with a joyful heart. Whether she met trouble at work or pressure at home, Xiaoling was always able to keep a joyful attitude.

One day Xiaoling met the greatest challenge of her life: she was diagnosed with a rare disease. The news left her shocked and afraid, but she did not give up her faith. She knew this was God's will, and she believed that God would walk with her on this journey.

Through prayer and thanksgiving, Xiaoling's mood gradually began to change. She learned to look for God's grace in difficulty, and thanked Him for His keeping and provision in every day. Even in the face of physical pain and inconvenience, Xiaoling was still able to radiate God's love and peace with a joyful heart.

We can learn a great deal from Xiaoling's story. Whatever difficulties and challenges we face, we can pray to God and thank Him for His presence and provision at every moment. Joy is not built on whether outward circumstances are good or bad, but on faith in God and gratitude for His grace.

So let us face the problems of life every day with a joyful heart. When we keep joy in the midst of difficulty, we show the world God's great power and love. At the same time, we become encouragement and hope to the people around us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you rejoice always every day, pray without ceasing, and give thanks in everything. May God's grace walk with you, may you find joy in difficulty, and may you become a witness to His love. Amen!

v: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
b: When we face sorrow and pressure in life, joy can become our good medicine. As this verse says, a joyful heart can heal our inner being and bring us vitality and health.

We live in a world filled with negative emotions and troubles. Sometimes we may be overwhelmed by crushing circumstances and the burdens of life. Yet in this verse God reminds us that joy is our strength against sorrow and weariness.

There was a young man named Weisheng who met many setbacks and failures at work. He felt very discouraged and helpless, and carried pressure and worry every day. Then one day he met a cheerful elder. The elder told Weisheng that joy was the secret of his success and happiness. Even in hard times he always found reasons to give thanks and embrace joy. This story inspired Weisheng, and he began to learn how to keep joy in difficulty. In the end, he overcame his setbacks, won success, and found true happiness.

This story tells us that whatever difficulty we are in, we can gain strength and healing from joy. Joy is more than an emotion; it is our connection with God, an expression of our trust in and obedience to Him. When we live out joy, we show the world God's love and power.

So let us choose every day to rejoice in the Lord. Whatever difficulties we meet, let us remember that the joy within is our good medicine. I bless you that you may gain strength from joy and bring forth faith and hope.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you radiate the light of joy every day. Amen!

v: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
b: In this world we often meet all kinds of difficulties and challenges. The pressures of life, problems in relationships, and even health challenges can all plunge us into sorrow. Yet when we turn to God and have His joy, we will find that this joy is our strength.

There was a child named Mingzong who often felt discouraged and powerless. His grades at school were poor, and friendships with classmates did not go well. But one day he heard a message about the joy of God. He began to learn to trust God and entrust his difficulties to Him. Every day he began to sing a joyful song of his own, and felt God's joy fill his soul.

As time passed, Mingzong began to find that he had become stronger and more positive. Although he still faced challenges, he learned from them to find the strength of joy in hardship. This joy not only let him see the other side of difficulty, but more importantly, it enabled him to share the joy with others, bringing them faith, hope, and love.

As the verse says, the joy of Yahweh is our strength. When we lay down our sorrows and entrust everything to God, His joy will fill our hearts. This joy can not only help us face difficulties, but also become the strength by which we influence others.
So let us seek God's joy every day and keep firm faith in the face of difficulty. When we live out this joy, we will be God's witnesses in this world, showing others His power and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's joy every day, and bring this joy to others. Amen!

v: Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.
b: This passage tells us that God gives light to the righteous and prepares gladness for the upright in heart. What a wonderful promise! In our lives, when we walk the path of righteousness, God will light our steps and prepare joy for us.

There was a boy named Weide who studied very hard at school, working diligently every day and finishing his homework. Though his classmates sometimes laughed at him as a bookworm, Weide held to his values and believed that effort was worthwhile.

One day the school held a big speech contest, and Weide decided to take part. He spent a lot of time researching the topic and wrote a splendid speech. On the day of the contest, Weide stood on the stage with a confident smile and began to speak.

His speech caught the attention of the whole hall, and everyone was moved by his deep and original insights. In the end, Weide won first place in the contest and became a figure everyone on campus noticed.

This story reminds us that when we pursue uprightness and righteous deeds, God lets our light spread and shine on those around us. Like Weide, when we work hard and believe in our own worth, we too can achieve amazing things.

In life we also face many challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we may feel discouraged, without hope or joy. But let us remember that God prepares gladness for the upright, for those who hold to righteous values. Even in hard times, we can know with confidence that God will give us the strength of joy and help us rise again.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep persevering on the path of pursuing righteousness and uprightness. May your life be like light spread abroad, lighting the way for others. May God prepare joy for you, so that in hard times you may have faith and hope. Amen!
Thank you all. May you enjoy this time of spiritual food. May God's word fill your hearts. Until we meet again, may the grace of the Lord be with you always. Amen!

v: You have loved righteousness, and hated wickedness. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.
b: Brothers and sisters, this passage reminds us that God loves righteousness and hates wickedness. He hopes that we too will look at the world and at our own actions with the same attitude. When we seek righteousness and stay away from evil, God will anoint us with the oil of gladness.

Imagine that when we are in the dark, a ray of joyful light suddenly shines ahead of us. This is God's anointing of gladness, giving us strength and courage to face the difficulties and trials of life. When we choose righteousness and refuse evil, God's gladness becomes our strength and motivation.

In life we may sometimes meet hardship and challenge. But let us remember that God's oil of gladness flows among us. It can give us courage and strength to overcome adversity. As the Bible says, God anointed us with the oil of gladness above our fellows.

It is like the story of a preacher who proclaimed the gospel in a village. But he met with many difficulties, and the people were full of hostility and suspicion toward him. Yet he insisted on choosing righteousness and kept proclaiming God's word. In the end, his joy and faithfulness moved people's hearts; they began to accept the gospel and built a deep relationship with Christ.

This story reminds us that when we face difficulties with an attitude of joy and righteousness, God's joy will be with us, giving us strength and courage. Whatever environment we are in, whatever difficulty we meet, the joy God gives can bring change and blessing.
pr: Lord, grant us joy, so that in all things we may live with righteousness and love. Bless us, Lord, so that we may become witnesses who proclaim righteousness and joy to the world.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you walk with God and find strength and hope in His joy. Amen!

v: The prospect of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
b: In this passage God reminds us how the hope of the righteous brings joy, while the hope of the wicked will surely perish. This is a very powerful and inspiring truth, so let us consider how to live it out in our lives.

We have all experienced disappointment and hardship, but as believers we must learn to place our hope in God. When we face difficulties with faith, we can see God's great power and salvation. Like Joseph in the Old Testament, who after being betrayed by his brothers and imprisoned still kept his hope in God, and in the end became prime minister of Egypt and saved his whole family.

There was a young girl named Yali, who came from a poor family but had a firm faith and hope for the future. Although life brought her many difficulties and challenges, she always believed that God would open a way for her. As a result, she studied hard and, through her effort, got into a famous university and became a successful doctor. Yali's story tells us that whatever our situation, as long as we keep faith and hope in God, He will surely lead us toward a bright future.

So let us remind ourselves every day that whatever difficulties we face, we can place our hope in God. At the same time, let us strive to keep our distance from the hope of the wicked, and not be deceived by the values of the world. For only in God can we find true joy and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you place your hope and faith in God every day, and face the challenges of life with joy and peace. Amen!

t: The Righteous Sing and Are Glad
v: An evil man is snared by his sin, but the righteous can sing and be glad.
b: In this verse we see a contrast between the wicked and the righteous. When the wicked sin, they are as if caught in a snare they cannot free themselves from. They use unrighteous behavior and evil deeds to gain profit, but in the end they only trap themselves in sin.

The righteous, by contrast, are full of joy and gladness. They choose to walk the path of righteousness and insist on doing what is right. The righteous understand that their joy comes not only from having escaped the snare of sin, but also from walking with God. The joy of the righteous springs from faith, hope, and love, and shines light and hope in life. It is like a person caught in the snare of drug abuse, unable to free himself. His life has become dark, full of despair and pain. Yet when he decides to quit the drugs and commit himself to the road of recovery, he will find a whole new world waiting for him. He will regain freedom and health, and find true joy in his life.

In the same way, when we choose to walk the path of righteousness and trust God's guidance, we will experience the joy of the righteous. This means not only that we can avoid the temptations of sin, but also that we have inner peace, hope, and satisfaction. When we draw near to God, listen to His word, and bring His love to the world around us, our lives will be set aflame and become a bright witness.

So let us choose joy every day and choose to walk the path of righteousness. Whatever difficulties and trials we face, let us remember that the joy of the righteous comes from our relationship with God, and is not affected by outward circumstances.
