When we live out light and joy, we will become guides in other people's lives, bringing them faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience the joy of the righteous every day, in good times and in bad. Amen!

t: Loving Wisdom Makes a Father Glad
v: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father; but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
b: In this passage we see two very different ways of behaving: one is loving wisdom, and the other is keeping company with prostitutes. The “prostitutes” spoken of here do not refer only to sex workers, but to everything that tempts us onto the wrong path.

We live in a world full of temptation and conflict. Every day we face a choice: to seek wisdom and love truth, or to let ourselves be bound by temptation and indulgence. This is an extremely important choice, because it affects not only our own lives, but is also directly related to the people around us.

There was a young man named Zhengxiang. From childhood Zhengxiang received a good education, and his father loved him very much and hoped he would have a bright future. But Zhengxiang fell in with the wrong circle of friends, who often went out to play and indulge in pleasure, neglecting study and growth.

His father saw the situation and was very worried and sad. He knew that if Peter did not change his way of life, he would waste his talent and opportunities. So he began to keep instilling in Zhengxiang the value of wisdom and truth, hoping he would find his direction again.

One day the father told Zhengxiang a story. He said, “Far away there was a young man who once lost his way as you have. He walked into a dark world, kept company with evil people, and wasted his money and time. Until one day he met a wise old man. This old man taught him how to choose the right road, to love truth and pursue wisdom.”

Listening to his father's words, Zhengxiang felt his heart touched. He began to think about his choices, and began to long to change his life. So he decided to leave those bad friends and seek wisdom and truth.

Some years later, Zhengxiang became a successful man. He had a happy family, and his father was very proud and glad of him. This story tells us that loving wisdom can make a father glad. On the other hand, the one who keeps company with prostitutes squanders his wealth. Here the prostitutes can be understood as everything that tempts us onto the wrong path.

In our lives there will also be many temptations and choices. Sometimes we may be deceived by worldly ideas and walk onto the wrong path. But when we love wisdom and pursue truth, we will find a whole new life.

Dear friends, let us reflect on our lives and ask ourselves: are we now loving wisdom or keeping company with prostitutes? Have we chosen thoughtful conduct and wise choices, or let ourselves be deceived by brief pleasure and temptation?

Remember, the conduct of loving wisdom not only makes a father glad, but also brings us a full life. When we pursue truth and choose the right road, we will find ourselves with more opportunities, more growth, and more satisfaction.

I bless you that you may go forward on the road of loving wisdom, far from temptation and indulgence. May you be children in whom that father takes pride and joy. May your lives be full of faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. Amen!

t: A Wise Son Makes a Glad Father
v: A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother.
b: In this passage we see how a wise son brings joy to his father, while a foolish man despises his mother. This passage tells us that our words and actions have a great influence on our parents.

There was a young man named Jiande. He was very enthusiastic about study and growth, and he brought his father great honor and joy. Every day Jiande studied hard, and he had the eyes of wisdom to look at things. Whether in school or in life, Jiande always achieved success with the right attitude and choices. His father, seeing how diligent and hardworking he was, felt very happy and proud. Jiande's wisdom became a bond between them and deepened their close relationship.

Now let us look at another story, about a young man named Yucheng, who did not value study and wisdom. He often acted rashly, without considering the consequences. He ignored his mother's advice and guidance, and turned a deaf ear to her opinions. His foolish and careless choices left his mother heartbroken and disappointed. This contempt led to distance in the family and created a gulf between parents and child.

These two stories tell us an important truth: a wise son makes a father glad. When we are willing to learn and grow, and to respect and listen to our parents' guidance, we can build better family relationships. Wisdom not only changes ourselves, but can also influence the whole family.

So let us strive to be wise children, and make our parents glad. Let us look at things with eyes of wisdom, and choose the right road. This will not only bring us success, but also give us a united and harmonious family.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be a wise child and a joy to your father and mother. May your words and actions bring your family faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!
b: In this passage we can see an important truth: a kind answer and a word spoken at the right time have great influence, and can make us ourselves feel joy and bring about good results.

Let us imagine a scene: one day as you are walking on the street, you meet a person who complains to you about his sufferings and troubles. You can choose to respond to him with kindness, listen to his heart, and give him encouragement and support. Then this person may feel warm and accepted, his mood will change as a result, and he will gain joy and hope.

On the other hand, if you choose to treat him coldly or rudely, he may feel discouraged and disappointed, and may sink even further into trouble. Our words and actions can have a great effect on other people's hearts, so we must learn to respond kindly and to speak encouraging and positive words at the right time.

This also applies to our daily interactions with family, friends, and colleagues. When we respond to them with a kind heart, listen to their needs, and give support, we can build better relationships and share moments of joy and goodness together.

Let us remember that a kind answer and a word in season can make ourselves feel joy, and can also plant seeds in other people's lives, letting them feel loved and valued. May we every day answer others with a kind tone and words spoken at the right time, bringing faith, hope, and love to one another.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you, in your dealings with people, show a kind attitude and timely responses, bringing joy and goodness to yourself and others. Amen!

t: Those Who Love the Lord Will Rejoice
v: You heard how I told you, ‘I am going away, and I will come back to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced because I said ‘I am going to my Father;’ for the Father is greater than I.
b: This passage reminds us that wherever we are, and whatever stage of life we are in, when we love the Lord Jesus Christ and believe His words, our hearts will be filled with joy.

There was a young man named Mark who lived in a poor area, and his family was not wealthy. Yet Mark had a heart full of faith and hope. He knew his present situation did not stand for his future, and he believed that as long as he worked hard, his dream could come true.

Mark often read in a small bookstore, and he was passionate about knowledge and learning. He often said to himself, “Although I am in poverty, I believe God will help me out of my difficulty.” He was determined to change his destiny.

Mark achieved excellent results in his studies and won a scholarship, giving him the chance to enter a famous university. But on the eve of entering university, his mother fell seriously ill and needed Mark's care and support.

Faced with this dilemma, Mark felt discouraged, but he did not give up hope. He knew he could not care for his mother and attend university at the same time, but he believed God would open a way for him.

At last Mark received sponsorship from afar, which could pay his tuition and living expenses. He could not only continue his education, but also take care of his duty to his mother. It was a miracle, and Mark felt great joy, because he knew it was God's love and care for him.
This story tells us that when we love the Lord and believe His words, we can be full of joy even in difficulty. Like Mark, his faith and hope let him witness God's great power and grace.
So wherever we are, and whatever stage of life we are in, as long as we love the Lord Jesus Christ, believe in Him and rely on Him, we can experience a life of joy and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you keep faith and hope in every difficulty, knowing that God is your helper. May you, like Mark, believe that even in hardship God is still with you, and that He has a good plan and purpose waiting for you. May your life be full of love, joy, and hope, and may you show the radiance of God every day. Amen!

v: Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.
b: In life we often meet difficulties and challenges that leave us feeling lost and discouraged. Sometimes we may ask ourselves: why do we have to go through this pain and sorrow?

This passage reminds us that although we may experience pain and sorrow, in the end that sorrow will be turned into joy. Just as a flower withers in winter yet blooms again beautifully in spring, we too can find joy out of sorrow.

There was a young athlete who lost both legs in a competition. He felt despair and sorrow, and could not imagine that he could have any hope left. Yet after a period of adjustment and effort, he regained his passion for life. He learned to use prosthetic legs and became a successful Paralympic athlete. His sorrow was turned into joy, and it inspired those around him.

We too can draw strength from this story: whatever difficulties and sorrows we meet, we can believe that they will bring new hope and joy. In this process we need firm faith and hope, believing that God will give us strength in our hardest moments.

Let us live out this joyful expectation, faith, and hope every day, refusing to yield in the face of difficulty, and believing that our sorrow will finally be turned into joy. Let us care for others with love, share joy and hope, and support one another.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find joy in difficulty and strength in sorrow. May your life be like a flower in full bloom, bursting forth with hope and love. Amen!

t: No One Can Take Your Joy
v: Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
b: This verse reminds us that even in sorrow we can have true joy.

In life there are many things that make us feel sorrow and disappointment, such as pressure at work, difficulties in relationships, or health problems. These things seem to take our joy away and leave us discouraged. Yet God's word reminds us that these situations are only temporary. When we meet the Lord again, He will give us true joy, and this joy is one that no one can take away.

It is like the delight of a child playing in an amusement park: when he meets a difficulty, he can recall that delight and understand that the difficulty is only temporary. This kind of joy comes from inner peace and hope for the future.

Through faith we can keep a joyful spirit. Just as the darkness of night cannot stop the dawn from coming, the challenges of life cannot stop us from having the joy God gives. When we face difficulties with faith, we can not only reach our goals, but also feel the presence of joy along the journey.

Please remember that in our daily lives we can experience the joy God gives. Whether in simple things, such as a cup of fragrant coffee, or in hard times, such as a good friend's encouragement, God is at our side, showing us His lovingkindness and faithfulness.
Let us keep a joyful spirit every day, believing that God's word is true, so that even in sorrow we can have true joy.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience the joy God gives every day. Amen!

v: to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may be glorified.
b: In life we cannot avoid facing hardship and sorrow, but this passage reminds us that God can turn our mourning into joy and exchange our sorrow for praise. These are truly uplifting and encouraging words.

There was a young man who lost the one he loved most, and it felt as if the whole world had collapsed; he fell into deep grief. Every day he was immersed in sorrow and could not come out of it. But one day he met a Christian friend whose testimony was optimism and hope.

This friend told him that even in the darkest days God can still turn sorrow into joy. He shared his own experience: when he lost a loved one, God gave him inner peace and joy, enabling him to stand up again and face life with a heart of praise.

The young man began to think, and decided to lay down his grief and open his heart to God, letting the Lord's joy fill his life. He learned to hand his mourning over to God, letting Him exchange it for the oil of joy, and letting the garment of praise take the place of the spirit of heaviness. Gradually his heart was filled with peace and joy, and he began to share this joy with others, and became, as it were, a tree of righteousness, showing the glory of the planting of Yahweh.

Dear family, we too can be like this young man, handing all our grief and sorrow over to God, and believing that He can turn them into joy and praise. When we face difficulties with a thankful and joyful heart, we can not only experience inner change, but also become a blessing to those around us.
So let us lay down all our sorrow, put on the garment of praise, and let the oil of joy fill our lives. May we, like trees of righteousness, radiate God's glory and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you find joy in difficulty, and become a blessing to those around you. Amen!

v: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,
b: “Peace to you, dear family. Welcome to enjoy a spiritual snack together. Today God's word says to us: ‘Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various trials.’” (James 1:2)

In this world we all meet all kinds of trials and difficulties. Sometimes we may feel discouraged, sad, or even desperate. Yet today's passage reminds us that when we face trials, we should meet them with a joyful spirit.

Imagine a child learning to ride a bicycle. At first he fell several times, cried from the pain, and felt very frustrated. But he did not give up. He resolutely stood up and got on the bike again. This time he kept his balance and rode off successfully. With a smile on his face, he was full of joy and a sense of accomplishment.

This story tells us that trials are like riding a bicycle. Like the child, when we face difficulties we can choose how to respond to them. We can choose to complain and give up, or we can choose to face them with a joyful attitude.

When we meet trials with a joyful spirit, we will find their value and meaning. These trials can help us grow, making us stronger and wiser. Just as gold needs to be refined in the fire, through trials we too can go through a process of reshaping and growth.

So whatever trials we face today, let us count it all joy. Let us no longer see trials as obstacles, but as opportunities for our growth. May we find God's grace and strength in difficulty, and keep going with a joyful heart.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you meet trials with a joyful spirit and gain growth and strength from them. Amen!
